subject: Art & Design
title: The Swinging Sixties: Youth Takes Over Fashion
description: Learn The Swinging Sixties: Youth Takes Over Fashion in one minute.

hook.text: Mary Quant's miniskirt shocked the world in 1964. Hemlines went to mid-thigh. Parents were horrified. Youth didn't care.

buildup.text: The 1960s shifted fashion power from Parisian couturiers to London's young designers. Youth culture drove the industry.

discovery.text: Pop art, space race aesthetics, and mod culture influenced fashion: bold patterns, geometric prints, PVC.

twist.text: André Courrèges also claims credit for the miniskirt. The debate is unresolved — but the revolution was undeniable.

climax.text: Twiggy became fashion's first supermodel at 16. The industry learned: youth sells, and it sells fast.

punchline.text: The sixties proved that fashion doesn't trickle down from elites.

quiz.question: How did the 1960s change the power structure of fashion?
options: Youth culture and London street fashion overtook Paris couture
Paris strengthened its dominance over global fashion
Fashion became less accessible to young people

details.summary: The 1960s transferred fashion power from Parisian couture houses to London's young designers. Mary Quant's miniskirt, André Courrèges' space-age looks, and Yves Saint Laurent's ready-to-wear democratized fashion, making youth culture the driving force of style for the first time.
details.whyItMatters: The sixties proved youth could lead fashion rather than follow it. This power shift — from elite couturiers to street culture — permanently changed how trends originate and spread.
takeaways: The 1960s shifted fashion power from Paris to London youth
Mary Quant's miniskirt symbolized a generational revolution
Ready-to-wear democratized fashion beyond elite couture

faq.question: Who actually invented the miniskirt?
faq.answer: Both Mary Quant in London and André Courrèges in Paris raised hemlines simultaneously in the early 1960s. Quant is more commonly credited because her King's Road boutique made short skirts accessible to young working women, while Courrèges presented them in haute couture.

faq.question: Why was youth culture suddenly so powerful in the 1960s?
faq.answer: The post-war baby boom created an enormous young demographic with disposable income and new cultural identity. Television spread trends instantly. Young people rejected their parents' styles, and designers who catered to this market gained unprecedented influence.
